title.en: US family reunited with pet cat seven years after it was lost: ‘We always thought about him’
title.zh: 美国家庭在宠物猫失踪七年后重逢：“我们一直想着它”

summary.en: A family cat named Dodger, lost during a move from California seven years ago, has been reunited with his humans at their new home in Georgia. The family had always thought about him, and he is reportedly settling back into his old ways.
summary.zh: 七年前，一个名叫道奇的家猫在从加利福尼亚搬家时走失，如今已在佐治亚州的新家与它的主人重逢。据报道，这家人一直惦记着它，而道奇也正在重新适应旧有的生活习惯。

body.en: Amber Davidson-Orozco said the family had lost Dodger, their cat, during their move out of California A family cat who got lost amid a move from California across the US is said to be settling back into his old ways with his humans at their new home in Georgia after experiencing an unlikely – but long hoped for – reunion more than seven years in the making. As owner Amber Davidson-Orozco put in an interview Wednesday, her cat Dodger still responds to his name and allows her sons to flip him playfully over their shoulders despite an absence from them that to the cat lasted the equivalent of roughly 24 years. Continue reading...

reflection.en: Seven years is a long time to mourn a lost pet, and this family's reunion with Dodger reminds us that even after extended periods of absence, joy can unexpectedly return. Psalm 30:5 beautifully captures this sentiment, where weeping gives way to rejoicing, even after a long night of waiting.
reflection.zh: 七年对于一只走失的宠物来说是很长的时间，这个家庭与道奇的重逢提醒我们，即使在漫长的分离之后，喜悦也能出乎意料地回归。诗篇30:5优美地捕捉了这种情感，即使在漫长的等待之夜后，哭泣也会让位给欢呼。

verse.textEn: Weeping may stay for the night, but rejoicing comes in the morning.
verse.textZh: 一宿虽然有哭泣，早晨便必欢呼。

title.en: 'I did not expect it': Kenya's Sabastian Sawe welcomed home with jubilant celebrations

summary.en: The first man to run a marathon in under two hours in a competitive race received a hero's welcome from supporters and family when he arrived home.
summary.zh: 首位在竞技马拉松比赛中跑进两小时的男子，在回到家乡时受到了支持者和家人的英雄般欢迎。

reflection.en: The jubilant welcome for Sabastian Sawe highlights the profound joy and admiration that accompany extraordinary human achievement. His historic feat reminds us of the dedication and perseverance required to run a race and secure the prize, inspiring us to pursue our own callings with similar commitment.
reflection.zh: 塞巴斯蒂安·萨韦所受到的热烈欢迎，彰显了非凡人类成就所带来的深刻喜悦和钦佩。他创造历史的壮举提醒我们，要跑完赛程并赢得奖赏，需要何等的奉献和毅力，激励我们以同样的决心去追求自己的使命。

verse.textEn: Do you not know that in a race all the runners run, but only one gets the prize? Run in such a way as to get the prize.
verse.textZh: 岂不知在场上赛跑的都跑，但得奖赏的只有一人？你们也当这样跑，好叫你们得着奖赏。

summary.en: The United Arab Emirates is leaving OPEC to pump more oil on its own terms. The break strips Saudi Arabia of a key partner and adds to growing uncertainty over the cartel's future.
summary.zh: 阿拉伯联合酋长国正退出欧佩克，以便按自己的条件开采更多石油。此举使沙特阿拉伯失去了一个关键伙伴，并增加了该卡特尔未来日益增长的不确定性。

reflection.en: The UAE's decision to leave OPEC to pursue its own oil production goals highlights the tension between individual gain and collective stability. This move, while perhaps economically advantageous for one party, creates uncertainty and weakens a long-standing partnership. Proverbs 15:17 reminds us that the value of harmonious relationships often outweighs...
reflection.zh: 阿联酋退出欧佩克以追求自身石油生产目标，这凸显了个人利益与集体稳定之间的张力。此举可能对一方有利，却给长期伙伴关系带来不确定性并削弱了它。箴言15:17提醒我们，和谐关系的价值往往超越对更多物质财富的追求。

verse.textEn: Better a small serving of vegetables with love than a fattened calf with hatred.

reflection.en: The journey of women journalists in Ghana highlights the persistent challenge of gender barriers in professional life. The biblical truth that in Christ there is "neither male nor female" reminds us of the inherent equality and dignity God bestows upon all, regardless of gender. This spiritual principle encourages us to dismantle societal structures that...
reflection.zh: 加纳女记者在职业生涯中克服性别障碍的经历，凸显了职场中性别壁垒的持续挑战。圣经真理指出，在基督里“不分男女”，这提醒我们雅伟上帝赋予所有人固有的平等和尊严，不分性别。这一属灵原则鼓励我们拆除限制任何人潜力的社会结构，并倡导一个让所有人都能蓬勃发展的环境。

verse.textEn: There is neither Jew nor Gentile, neither slave nor free, nor is there male and female, for you are all one in Christ Jesus.
verse.textZh: 并不分犹太人、希利尼人，自主的、为奴的，或男或女，因为你们在基督耶稣里都成为一了。

title.en: King and Queen lay flowers at 9/11 Memorial in New York

summary.en: King Charles and Queen Camilla visited the 9/11 Memorial in New York during their state visit to the US, laying flowers in remembrance.
summary.zh: 查尔斯国王和卡米拉王后在美国进行国事访问期间，参观了纽约的9/11纪念馆并献花致意。

reflection.en: Visiting a memorial for such a profound loss reminds us of the deep sorrow that follows tragedy. The simple act of laying flowers acknowledges the tears shed and the lives forever changed by such events, echoing the profound empathy shown in Scripture.
reflection.zh: 参观如此巨大的损失纪念馆，提醒我们悲剧过后深沉的悲痛。献花的简单举动，承认了因这些事件而流下的泪水和永远改变的生命，这与圣经中展现的深切同情心相呼应。

body.en: Human rights commissioner says alleged jailing highlights the ‘growing risks of transnational repression’ in Australia Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast Australia’s human rights commissioner has said the Chinese student who was allegedly jailed for six years by Chinese authorities for joining protests in Sydney underscores the “very real and growing risks of transnational repression affecting people in Australia – including international students”. Commissioner Lorraine Finlay told Guardian Australia that while she could not comment on the circumstances of individual cases “no one should fear punishment abroad for exercising their lawful rights to free expression and peaceful protest here”.
